verifiable-quality-gates.why: the change ships a discrimination test proven to fail when the fix is neutralized: stashing the esk-genesis refresh (reverting it to no-clobber) makes the consumer-lifecycle test fail on the exact 'hook was not refreshed' assertion
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added test/consumer-lifecycle.test.mjs that installs a consumer, stales its hook and workflow, re-runs esk-genesis, and asserts both refresh; verified it fails when esk-genesis is reverted to no-clobber
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: the change is architecturally significant (which installer-written files refresh on upgrade versus stay no-clobber, and why) and is recorded in one ADR with the code
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0069 documenting the no-clobber upgrade bug, the owned-versus-consumer-owned refresh rule, the consumer-lifecycle test, and the honest limits
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the upgrade behavior gained a non-happy path (an existing consumer whose owned files are stale) that was enumerated and committed as an executable test
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added the stale-hook-and-workflow upgrade scenario as a node:test case, following the repo's discrimination-test convention
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: a .mjs behavior change fired the behavior-change coupling; the fix is pinned at the level that catches it, an installer integration test that runs esk-genesis end to end against a temp consumer
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: pinned the upgrade-refresh fix with an integration test that runs the real esk-genesis twice against a throwaway consumer and asserts the owned files refresh
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

skeptical-audit.why: the fix claim is backed by a re-runnable reproduction (stash the fix, run the test, see it fail on the exact assertion), and the ADR and changelog state the honest limits (the test simulates the prior release by staling files, and the vendored-skills topology is not yet covered)
skeptical-audit.what: proved the discrimination by stashing the esk-genesis change and observing the test fail, then restored it, and recorded the verification limits in the ADR
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

release-deployment-safety.why: the whole change is about the upgrade path: making re-running esk-genesis deliver fixes to an existing consumer, backward-compatible, with the gate set unchanged, shipped as a 1.2.2 patch
release-deployment-safety.what: made esk-genesis refresh owned files on re-run so a consumer upgrade actually lands the fix, kept consumer-owned files no-clobber, and bumped the version as a backward-compatible patch
quotes: Every change must be independently deployable, backward-compatible, observable while it rolls out

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review was run on the change before opening the PR, against the four questions, and recorded in the arch-review log
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in a fresh subagent over the esk-genesis change and the new test, resolved findings, and recorded the review in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

arch-encode.why: no new greppable rule to encode into a rules file; the change refreshes existing installer-written files and is enforced by a discrimination test, not by a new rules-file entry

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no PII, retention, migration, backup or audit logic changed; this is installer file-write logic and a test

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system, service, database or integration architecture changed; this adjusts which installer-written files refresh on upgrade

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no input, auth, session, crypto, upload or dependency surface changed; the installer copies the same template with no shell

pattern-selector.why: no new feature, class, module or data flow; the change reuses the existing refresh-on-hash-diff pattern already used for apply-ruleset.sh and the gate scripts

sre-operational-readiness.why: no SLI/SLO, alert, runbook or production-operability surface changed

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing or UI surface; this is installer machinery, a test, a manifest and docs

universal-browser-device-support.why: no frontend or browser-facing code; this is developer-facing installer tooling

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing flow, screen, form or copy; this is developer-facing installer tooling and documentation
